meta.format: findings explained by severity with concrete remediation recommendations (mirrors AUDIT.md)

verdict.summary: No known exploitable application-level vulnerability. Credential storage fix verified and shipped. Release gate requires the 7-day pipeline-hardening items (branch protection, approval-gated signed release publishing, SHA-pinned release actions, signing-key isolation, docs refresh).

findings.title: No branch protection on main + zero-approval signed release publishing
findings.evidence: branch protection API returns 404; version-bump.yml has permissions contents:write and auto-pushes to main; release.yml auto-publishes signed release on any v*/beta* tag push
findings.explanation: Three facts combine into one exploit chain: (1) gh api repos/jaydenrussell/CallerFlash/branches/main/protection returns 404, so main has no branch protection, required PR, status check, signature requirement, or push restriction; (2) version-bump.yml runs on every push to main with contents:write and pushes a 'chore: bump' commit itself, so any actor who can push to main can also push a v*/beta* tag; (3) release.yml triggers on any such tag and auto-publishes a public release with draft:false, no environment, and no approval gate, generating the minisign signature and update.json the updater trusts. Because update artifacts are signed with TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY (a repo secret), an attacker who compromises the GitHub account or a maintainer PAT can land malicious code, push a tag, auto-publish a signed malicious installer, and all users auto-update to it. Write access additionally permits editing release.yml itself to exfiltrate the signing key: full, silent supply-chain takeover.
findings.recommendation: Do all together: (1) enable branch protection on main: gh api -X PUT repos/jaydenrussell/CallerFlash/branches/main/protection -f required_status_checks[strict]=true -f required_status_checks[contexts][]=lint-build -f required_status_checks[contexts][]=rust -f required_pull_request_reviews[required_approving_review_count]=1 -f enforce_admins=true -f required_signatures=true -f allow_force_pushes=false -f allow_deletions=false; then restrict direct pushes so only a callerflash-bot fine-grained least-privilege PAT scoped to this repo can push bump commits. (2) Move TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY + password into a GitHub environment named 'release' with required_reviewers and reference it from the release job (environment: release + contents: write). (3) Publish as draft and promote manually, or keep auto-publish behind the approval environment. (4) Add actions/attest-build-provenance (SHA-pinned) to bind artifacts to the exact run. (5) Rotate the minisign signing key after the environment is in place. (6) Prefer gh release create over softprops/action-gh-release to remove the third-party action: gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" artifacts/** --generate-notes --verify-tag (add --prerelease only when the tag contains -beta).

findings.title: release.yml unpinned actions, broad permissions, non-reproducible build
findings.evidence: checkout@v3, setup-node@v4, softprops/action-gh-release@v1 floating tags; workflow-level contents:write; choco packages unpinned; PJSIP built from moving HEAD git clone
findings.explanation: ci.yml correctly pins checkout and setup-node by SHA, but release.yml uses floating tags (actions/checkout@v3, actions/setup-node@v4, softprops/action-gh-release@v1, upload/download-artifact@v4). A floating tag can be silently repointed by its upstream owner, changing what the release build runs. The workflow also grants workflow-level contents:write (the build job needs none), choco install pulls unpinned package versions, and PJSIP is built from git clone https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject.git, i.e. the moving HEAD of the upstream repo, making every release build non-reproducible and exposed to upstream compromise.
findings.recommendation: (1) Pin every action by SHA, reusing the pins proven in ci.yml and resolving the rest via dependabot update-types:[pin] or gh api: - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 (v4); - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 (v4). (2) Scope permissions to jobs: build -> contents: read; only the release job gets contents: write. (3) Pin PJSIP to a released tag/commit: git clone --branch <pjsip-release-tag> --depth 1 https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject.git /tmp/pjproject; pin choco versions (choco install msys2 --version=X.Y); cache the PJSIP build output with actions/cache.

findings.title: Windows Authenticode signing configured but not wired into release.yml
findings.evidence: WIN_CSC_LINK and WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD secrets present but no signCommand and no signing env in release.yml
findings.explanation: WIN_CSC_LINK and WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD secrets exist, but the Tauri build step never uses them: tauri.conf.json has no signCommand and release.yml sets only the updater-signing env. The shipped .exe is therefore not Authenticode-signed: Windows shows a SmartScreen 'unknown publisher' warning, the installer's only authenticity is the minisign signature the updater verifies, enterprises cannot deploy via MDM, and a tampered installer downloaded outside the updater is indistinguishable from a legit one.
findings.recommendation: Sign the installer during bundling. In tauri.conf.json bundle.windows.nsis add: "signCommand": "signtool sign /fd SHA256 /f \"%WIN_CSC_LINK%\" /p \"%WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD%\" /tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 \"%1\"". Keep TAURI_SIGNING_* for updater signatures (the two layers are independent). Validate on a test release before the next stable.

findings.title: WebView CSP defense-in-depth gaps
findings.evidence: style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval' with no wasm bundle; connect-src includes github hosts only needed for beta endpoint fetch; no CSP violation reporting
findings.explanation: The CSP allows style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com 'unsafe-inline', which inline styles can abuse for data-exfiltration via CSS attribute selectors + background:url(...) if any script injection occurs; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' permits wasm compilation although the production bundle contains no wasm, so the allowance is pure risk; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com https://github.com https://objects.githubusercontent.com exists only for the beta-endpoint fetch in tauri-bridge.ts (the real update check runs in Rust), so these hosts become an exfiltration sink if a renderer script ever runs; and there is no report-to, so injection attempts and policy violations are invisible. The toast window (toast.html) keeps 'unsafe-inline' for its inline <style>; it is an isolated webview with no user input, so this is acceptable but closable by moving styles to an external file.
findings.recommendation: (1) Move beta-endpoint resolution into a Rust command (cmd_check_update already has a validated endpoint). (2) Tighten the CSP to: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com data:; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'. Verify the Tailwind build emits only external CSS. (3) Add CSP violation reporting routed to the diagnostics log (Tauri supports a custom CSP handler). (4) Optionally move toast.html's <style> block to external CSS and drop 'unsafe-inline' there too.

findings.title: Security documentation describes a different app than shipped
findings.evidence: SECURITY.md documents keyring AES-256-GCM + openssl Ed25519 signing; reality is DPAPI + minisign. cmd_verify_update and VERIFY_PUBLIC_KEY_B64 are dead code (no frontend caller); RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY unused
findings.explanation: SECURITY.md says credentials are AES-256-GCM under a keyring and releases are signed with OpenSSL Ed25519 detached signatures. Shipped reality: credentials are DPAPI-encrypted (storage.rs/secure.rs) and releases are minisign-signed via tauri-plugin-updater. cmd_verify_update and its hard-coded Ed25519 key are dead code with no frontend caller, and RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY is unused. Anyone reading the docs (auditor, researcher, future agent) will model the wrong trust root and may miss the real one (the minisign key).
findings.recommendation: (1) Rewrite SECURITY.md to match reality: DPAPI at rest (Windows-only, user-bound), minisign updater signing with the pinned pubkey in tauri.conf.json, version monotonicity. (2) Delete cmd_verify_update, VERIFY_PUBLIC_KEY_B64, the pub use in lib.rs, and the unused RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secret. (3) Document the minisign key as the single release trust root plus its rotation/recovery procedure.

findings.title: Raw error tails still reach the renderer
findings.evidence: user_safe_sip_error fallback returns 'SIP error: <raw up to 128 chars>'
findings.explanation: user_safe_sip_error maps common OS/DNS errors to friendly text, but the fallback branch returns 'SIP error: {raw up to 128 chars}', so unmapped errors can expose host/IP/port/OS details in the UI and in the on-disk diagnostics file.
findings.recommendation: Make the fallback fully generic (e.g. 'SIP registration failed - check server and port'); keep the raw detail only in the Rust-side log::error!; remove the 'SIP error: {}' format entirely.

findings.title: Legacy migration key derivation not secret
findings.evidence: derive_machine_key derives AES key from hostname+arch+cpu (non-secret) for enc:/fb: formats
findings.explanation: Legacy Sip-Toast enc:/fb: formats derive the AES key from non-secret values (hostname + platform + arch + CPU model). Anyone with the ciphertext can recompute the key and decrypt old passwords. This only affects one-time migration of legacy data; new data is DPAPI-protected, but it should never be presented as secure.
findings.recommendation: Document the limitation in SECURITY.md; after a successful migration delete the legacy config file(s) (run_migration is idempotent via the marker file); never log plaintext (already enforced by the redaction chokepoint).

findings.title: No coverage gate; thin bridge/IPC test coverage
findings.evidence: unit tests for storage/sip/startup/redaction exist; no coverage threshold; tauri-bridge.ts untested
findings.explanation: Unit tests exist for storage, SIP config validation, startup, host_is_private, and redaction, but there is no coverage threshold and the IPC layer (tauri-bridge.ts: sanitizers, endpoint resolution, error mapping, SecureStorage) has no tests - the exact layer where the 1.9.5 regression lived.
findings.recommendation: Add a coverage job with a threshold (cargo llvm-cov for Rust, vitest --coverage with a floor for TS) and add unit tests for sanitizeSipServer, resolveUpdateEndpoint (stable/beta), bridge error mapping, and SecureStorage write-queue behavior.

findings.title: Panic hook writes raw panic payload to plaintext files
findings.evidence: writes raw panic message + process args to %APPDATA% and %TEMP%
findings.explanation: The global panic hook writes the raw panic message and process args to %APPDATA%\CallerFlash\crashes\ and %TEMP%. If a future panic ever formats a secret (e.g. a debug {:?} of a config), it would persist to disk in plaintext. There is also no crash-collection path.
findings.recommendation: Run the panic text through a redaction pass before writing; drop the %TEMP% copy (or restrict it to debug builds); consider optional, consent-based crash reporting later.

findings.title: Rate limiter mutex poisoning + in-memory only
findings.evidence: Mutex::unwrap() panics on poisoning; per-process in-memory buckets
findings.explanation: self.buckets.lock().unwrap() will panic if a thread panics while holding the lock, turning a benign failure into a crash. The limiter is per-process and in-memory, which is fine for a single-user desktop app (its job is to stop a compromised renderer from spamming IPC) but should be documented as such.
findings.recommendation: Use self.buckets.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()); add a comment that the limiter's scope is renderer-spam containment.

findings.title: No integrity check on settings.json non-secret fields
findings.explanation: settings.json has atomic writes, a backup file, and JSON-parse validation, but no integrity/HMAC over non-secret fields. A local actor could edit e.g. toastConfig or appPreferences undetected. Impact is limited to the same OS user (who can already operate as that user) and credentials stay DPAPI-protected, so this is an accepted-risk candidate.
findings.recommendation: Either document as accepted (preferred) or add an HMAC over non-secret fields, with the explicit constraint that the HMAC key must not be weaker than DPAPI, otherwise it adds nothing.

findings.title: npm audit gate only at high; current tree has 1 high dev vuln
findings.evidence: undici 7.28.0 high (dev-only via jsdom); dependabot PR to 7.29.0 open and CI-green
findings.explanation: npm audit --audit-level=high ignores moderate/low advisories. A live audit of main reports undici 7.28.0 high (dev-only, pulled in by jsdom); a dependabot PR bumping to 7.29.0 is open and CI-green. Runtime impact is nil (dev-only), but the gate would currently pass despite a pending high advisory.
findings.recommendation: Merge the dependabot PR; consider --audit-level=moderate once dev advisories are auto-managed; keep npm audit failing-fast so pending advisories surface.

findings.title: Auto version bump does not sync Cargo.lock
findings.evidence: bumps Cargo.toml/package.json/tauri.conf.json only; root-package version in Cargo.lock drifts
findings.explanation: The auto-bump rewrites Cargo.toml, package.json, and tauri.conf.json but not the root-package version entry in Cargo.lock, so the committed lockfile drifts from the manifest after every bump (the release build rewrites it in-place on the runner, hiding the drift).
findings.recommendation: In the bump step, also replace the root package version in Cargo.lock (or run cargo check --locked on the runner and commit the result).

findings.title: Stale governance artifacts contradict real workflow
findings.evidence: describe refactor/tauri branch, gh-API-only edits, NO LOCAL BUILDS, temp working dir; actual ops are main + local checkout + local tsc/lint
findings.explanation: Both AGENTS.md and CRITICAL.md describe a nonexistent model (refactor/tauri branch, gh-API-only edits, NO LOCAL BUILDS, temp working dir). Actual operations use main, a direct local checkout, and local tsc/lint. Agents and contributors following the docs will take wrong actions.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite both to the real operating model (main branch, local checkout, tsc --noEmit / npm run lint / cargo test allowed, builds validated by CI).

findings.title: Diagnostics file persists server host/port and SIP usernames
findings.evidence: sip:log and migration messages include server:port and usernames (never passwords)
findings.explanation: The on-disk diagnostics log intentionally stores support-relevant detail (server:port, usernames) but never passwords (redaction chokepoint). The exported log is therefore sensitive and may contain the account owner's PII.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'clear diagnostics' action that also deletes the on-disk diagnostics.log; document the file's contents in the UI.

findings.title: Update endpoint is a mutable GitHub pointer
findings.evidence: releases/latest/download/update.json; integrity preserved by minisign verification
findings.explanation: releases/latest/download/update.json is a mutable pointer: GitHub's 'latest' can be re-pointed or a release replaced. Integrity is preserved because the updater verifies the minisign signature against the pinned pubkey - defense-in-depth, not a bypass. Worth hardening for a mature product.
findings.recommendation: Serve update.json and installers from immutable storage or a dedicated endpoint (per the releases.callerflash.app intent in SECURITY.md), and publish a documented minisign key-rotation/recovery procedure.

resolved_since_last_audit: C1 plaintext password -> DPAPI at rest
C3 SIP header injection -> dangerous-char validation
C5 unsanitized caller name -> sanitizeCallerName + parser-exit sanitizer
C9 CI lockfile deletion + npm install -> npm ci
C10 CI never ran tests -> npm test + cargo test
H7 broad shell:allow-open -> HTTPS-only + Rust validation + private-host block
H8 cargo audit continue-on-error -> fails CI
H10 no SAST -> CodeQL active (rust), 0 findings
M5 toast payload -> 64KB cap + object check
